formalDefinition: SAT = {Φ | Φ is a satisfiable Boolean formula}
problemDefinition: SAT, or the Boolean satisfiability problem, is a problem that asks for a list of assignments to the literals of phi to result in 'True'
outputDescription: True or False, whether Φ is satisfiable
source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
instanceFormat: Boolean formula. Clauses joined by '&', literals within a clause joined by '|', negation prefix '!' written directly before the name. Variable names start with a letter or '_' and contain only letters, digits and '_'. When there are several clauses, each clause with more than one literal must be in parentheses. Each clause has 1+ literals of any size. Example: (x1 | !x2 | x3) & (!x1 | x2)
certificateFormat: Comma-separated variable:value pairs, optionally wrapped in parentheses. Booleans must be capitalized True/False (T/F also accepted); ':' or '=' may be used as the separator. List every variable you are assigning. Example: (x1:True,x2:False,x3:True)

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This is a simple brute force solver for SAT

timeComplexity.Description: , n = number of variables, |phi| = formula size
